faq.q: Why does pressure increase with depth?
faq.a: Water pressure comes from the weight of the water above you. The deeper you go, the more water is stacked above, so the pressure grows steadily, about one extra atmosphere every 10 metres.

faq.q: Why do my ears hurt at the bottom of a pool?
faq.a: Water pressure pushes your eardrum inward, while the air behind it is still at surface pressure. Swallowing, or gently blowing with your nose pinched, lets air into the middle ear to balance it.
asks: How do divers stop ear pain?

faq.a: Breath-hold divers have reached over 200 metres, and scuba divers breathing special gas mixtures over 300 metres. Deeper than that, people need submarines with very thick walls.
asks: What is the deepest anyone has dived?

faq.q: How do deep-sea animals survive the pressure?
faq.a: Their bodies are mostly water, which hardly squashes, and many have no air-filled spaces to crush. The pressure inside them matches the pressure outside, so it pushes equally both ways.

faq.q: How deep is the deepest part of the ocean?
faq.a: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, in the Pacific Ocean, is about 10,900 metres deep. The pressure there is more than 1,000 times the pressure at the surface.

facts: In sea water, pressure increases by about one atmosphere for every 10 metres of depth.
The Challenger Deep, the deepest known point of the ocean, is about 10,900 metres deep.
Water is about 800 times denser than air at sea level.

quiz.say: A diver swims down from the surface to 10 metres deep. What happens to the pressure on her?
quiz.show: From the surface to 10 metres deep, the pressure…
quiz.why: At the surface the air gives 1 atmosphere; 10 metres of water adds about 1 more, making about 2 atmospheres.

wrong.0: The weight of the water above adds pressure as you go down.
wrong.2: Pressure grows with depth; it never drops as you go deeper.
